newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Babayevskoye candy factory to issue shares.
newsitem.headline: Russian Babayevskoye candy factory to issue shares.

text.p: AO Babayevskoye, one of Russia's biggest confectioners, will raise its authorised capital by 20 percent from the current amount of 139.4 million roubles, the agent for the issue said.
The new issue will be placed among Russian and foreign investors at the end of October or start of November, Inna Klyshevich from Inkom-Kapital, told Reuters.
She refused to mention the selling price. The face value of a share is five roubles.
She said Babayevskoye was in talks with potential investors.

AB Inkombank and its affiliates is the main shareholder of Babayevskoye with 67.5 percent of shares, five percent was allocated to the employees' fund, Babayevskoye itself holds 14.5 percent of shares, OOO Finansovye Sistemy has a 6.8 percent stake and households have 6.2 percent of shares.
Babayevskoye's 1995 net profit was over $25 million, Klyshevich said.

The revenues from the share issue will be used to set up a consortium of confectionery producers, which will unite several regional producers. They will have a single marketing, financial and industrial systems, Klyshevich said.
The project also provides for equipment modernisation at all companies, she said.
She refused to say which other companies would join the consortium.
Babayevskoye has worked out an $8 million 3-5 year modernisation programme to be funded from the proceeds of the share sale, she said.
